candidate.answerReason: Jill takes 6 minutes and Jack takes 15 minutes. Because they leave together, Jill arrives 9 minutes earlier.

methods.label: Compare travel times
methods.explanation:
Because Jack and Jill leave together, the difference in their travel times is also the difference in their arrival times.

Jill travels \(10\) miles in \(60\) minutes at a constant speed, so her one-mile trip takes \(60\div10=6\) minutes. Jack travels \(4\) miles in \(60\) minutes, so his one-mile trip takes \(60\div4=15\) minutes. Thus Jill arrives
\[
15-6=9\text{ minutes}
\]
before Jack. The answer is \(\boxed{9}\) minutes, choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses constant-speed reasoning, division, hour-to-minute conversion, and subtraction.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task applies the distance-speed-time relationship and converts hours to minutes. Recovering travel time by division uses the inverse multiplication relationship in cnm_p110. No meeting or catching-up analysis is needed.

review.mathematicalCheck: The travel times are \(60/10=6\) and \(60/4=15\) minutes. Simultaneous departure makes the arrival difference \(15-6=9\) minutes, choice D.
review.levelCheck: Elementary division, time conversion, and subtraction fit AMC 8. The explanation connects travel times to arrival times.
